Tarczyn Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tarczyn, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Tarczyn developed after 1795, growing from 126 residents in 1808 to 1,427 (56% of the population) by 1921. Notable rabbis Josef Horowitz of Lublin and Jechiel Dancygier both resided there. In February 1941, Tarczyn's Jews were deported to the Warsaw Ghetto, and most were murdered at Treblinka the following year. The cemetery's exact founding date is unknown, though burial-fee records from 1847-1849 suggest it predates that; its oldest identified tombstone is dated 1855. Roughly half the cemetery was later converted to farmland, the rest to an illegal dump, and nearly all tombstones were removed over the following decades. Since 2016, local volunteers have cleared rubbish and vegetation, persuaded farmers to stop using the land, and erected a partial concrete fence in 2018. About 30 sandstone tombstones survive today, most moved from their original burial locations.
